facts.statement: A partial skeleton of Yixianosaurus was discovered in 2001 at Wangjiagou in Liaoning, northeastern China.
facts.quote: Its partial skeleton was discovered in 2001, in Liaoning at Wangjiagou in northeastern China.

facts.statement: The known fossil material includes a shoulder girdle, complete fossilized arms with feathers, some ribs, and gastralia.
facts.quote: It consists of the shoulder girdle and a pair of fossilized arms complete with fossilized feathers, some ribs, and gastralia.

facts.statement: Yixianosaurus possessed a very long hand measuring 140% of the length of its 89 mm humerus.
facts.quote: Yixianosaurus has a very long hand, 140% of the length of the 89 mm humerus.

facts.statement: The second finger of Yixianosaurus is the longest among its digits.
facts.quote: The second finger is the longest.

facts.statement: The fingers of Yixianosaurus bear large and recurved claws.
facts.quote: The fingers bear large and recurved claws.

facts.statement: The estimated total body length of Yixianosaurus is 1 meter and its weight is 1 kilogram.
facts.quote: The total body length has been estimated at 1 m, the weight at 1 kg.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that large pennaceous feathers on the forelimbs indicate Yixianosaurus was adapted for limited aerial locomotion.
facts.quote: Xu et al. (2013) suggested that the presence of large pennaceous feathers on parts of the forelimb strongly supports that Yixianosaurus was adapted for limited aerial locomotion.

facts.statement: Yixianosaurus likely lived during the early Aptian stage, approximately 122 million years ago.
facts.quote: which likely derived from the Dawangzhangzi Bed (early Aptian stage, 122 million years ago).

facts.statement: The original describers suggested Yixianosaurus was a close relative of the Scansoriopterygidae.
facts.quote: they suggested it was a close relative of the Scansoriopterygidae.

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that Yixianosaurus may belong to the dromaeosaurid group.
facts.quote: Other researchers have suggested the specimen may have come from a dromaeosaurid.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Yixianosaurus is a primitive dinosaur outside the Eumaniraptora clade or a basal member of the Paraves.
facts.quote: Subsequent analyses were divided on whether is it is more primitive and outside the clade Eumaniraptora – this would mean that advanced characteristics such as the long hands and short arms evolved independently in this species – or a basal member of the more advanced Paraves.

facts.statement: Yixianosaurus is classified within the unranked family Maniraptora.
Yixianosaurus is classified within the family Anchiornithidae.
Yixianosaurus lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, 122 million years ago during the Aptian, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace 122 millones de años durante el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: A 2017 re-evaluation determined that Yixianosaurus was the most basal paravian.
facts.quote: Una revaluación de 2017 del espécimen de Archaeopteryx de Harlem llevó a determinar que era un anquiornítido llamado Ostromia, mientras que se determinó que Yixianosaurus sería el paraviano más basal.

facts.statement: The time range for Yixianosaurus is estimated from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species Yixianosaurus longimanus was formally named and described by Xu Xing and Wang Xiaolin in 2003.
rejected.quote: The type species, Yixianosaurus longimanus, was formally named and described by Xu Xing and Wang Xiaolin in 2003.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'species Yixianosaurus longimanus was formally named and described'

rejected.statement: Two studies published in 2017 argued that Yixianosaurus was more closely related to Xiaotingia, with both genera being either scansoriopterygid relatives or anchiornithids.
rejected.quote: Sin embargo, dos otros estudios publicados durante el mismo año afirmaron que Yixianosaurus estaba más cercanamente relacionado con Xiaotingia, siendo ambos géneros parientes cercanos de los escansoriopterígidos o serían anquiornítidos.
